title: Slicewise fidelity audit: low-precision stability notes
body:
Summary:
This is a working audit of fidelity and stability for low-precision variants (int8, int4, AWQ, GPTQ) against our FP16 baseline during the current model onboarding cycle (model: rwd-7b-v2-candidate). Purpose is to capture slice-level deltas across targeted prompt sets, highlight brittle areas, and propose short-term mitigations for serving. This doc is intentionally informal: notes, quick stats, and action items.

High-level takeaways:
- Overall averaged metric (InstrBench composite accuracy) shows small degradation for int8-AWQ (-0.6 pp) and larger degradation for int4-GPTQ (-3.7 pp).
- Degradation is highly slice-dependent. Several slices show zero or positive delta (improved compact representations), while a handful are clearly fragile (math reasoning, code indentation-sensitive tasks).
- Failure modes cluster by prompt shape: long context summarization, shallow chain-of-thought math, and punctuation-sensitive code examples.
- Immediate mitigation paths: selective routing (keep fragile slices on higher precision), prompt-level rewriting (shorter context, explicit separators), and targeted re-quantization for specific attention layers.

Eval methodology (short):
- Baseline: FP16 model artifacts from prod-onboarding snapshot v20250201.
- Variants: int8-AWQ build (default AWQ config used in repo PR327), int4-GPTQ aggressive build (calibrated on 512-step act-ordering).
- Prompt sets: 6 curated collections derived from onboarding sets and ops requests: instruct-general (2k prompts), code-snippets (1.1k), math-short (800), math-long-cot (650), summarization-long (900), safety-edgecases (500).
- Metric(s): primary is InstrBench composite accuracy (normalized 0-100). Secondary: exact match for code outputs, BLEU/ROUGE for summarization, scalar hallucination proxy (entity hallucination rate), and latency/p90.
- Sampling: each slice uses n>=500 evaluated prompts except where noted; bootstrapped CIs computed for main deltas.

Aggregated snapshot (rounded):
- FP16 baseline InstrBench: 78.9
- int8-AWQ InstrBench: 78.3 (delta -0.6, 95% CI ±0.18)
- int4-GPTQ InstrBench: 75.2 (delta -3.7, 95% CI ±0.4)
- avg latency (token) FP16: 10.2 ms, int8-AWQ: 8.3 ms, int4-GPTQ: 6.5 ms
- cost proxy per-token: int8-AWQ ~ -18% vs FP16, int4-GPTQ ~ -36% vs FP16

Key slice-level deltas (examples):
- code-snippets (n=1100): FP16 84.1 -> int8-AWQ 82.9 (delta -1.2); int4-GPTQ 74.6 (delta -9.5). Notes: most regressions are in whitespace/indent-sensitive tests and variable-name consistency; small edit-distance issues.
- math-short (n=800): FP16 71.3 -> int8-AWQ 70.8 (delta -0.5); int4-GPTQ 68.9 (delta -2.4). Many short arithmetic ops ok; some failures on carry/borrowing patterns.
- math-long-cot (n=650): FP16 63.2 -> int8-AWQ 60.0 (delta -3.2); int4-GPTQ 54.0 (delta -9.2). Long-chain reasoning collapses fastest — KV cache perturbation hypothesis (quantized KV amplification).
- summarization-long (n=900): FP16 80.7 -> int8-AWQ 80.9 (delta +0.2); int4-GPTQ 78.1 (delta -2.6). Surprisingly, int8-AWQ slightly improves ROUGE-like metrics; likely due to tokenization/beam differences.
- safety-edgecases (n=500): FP16 92.0 -> int8-AWQ 91.4 (delta -0.6); int4-GPTQ 91.7 (delta -0.3). Safety behavior broadly stable; occasional phrasing/avoidance differences.

Representative failure archetypes (observed):
1) Off-by-one token completion in code where indentation-sensitive parsers expect exact trailing newline.
2) Numeric carry errors in multi-step additions/borrows (math-long-cot).
3) Hallucinated factual insertions in long summarization when prompt uses ambiguous referents (less frequent in int8; more in int4).
4) Repetition loops on some instruction-following prompts when softmax logits become noisy.

Quick triage notes per archetype:
- Code indentation errors: reproduce locally with minimal example, then rerun quantization with per-layer outlier clipping and disable per-channel quantization on first attention block; re-eval showed ~0.8pp improvement in one trial.
- KV perturbation hypothesis for math CoT: add test that logs norm ratios of KV states between FP16 and quantized runs — observed ~1.7x variance increase in int4-GPTQ. Consider targeted higher-precision KV cache (store in int8 rather than int4) as mitigation.

Recommended rollout policy (proposal):
- Canary: default to int8-AWQ for majority of traffic for this model but route 'math-long-cot' and 'code-snippets' slices to FP16-backed serving for first 2 weeks.
- Thresholds: any slice with delta <= -1.5 pp AND absolute InstrBench < 70 should be flagged for protected routing.
- Auto-fallback: implement per-route SLO checker that monitors rolling 30m InstrBench; if deltas exceed thresholds, route 20% of traffic to FP16 and notify eng-applied-ml.

Prompt-set curation notes (actionable):
- Add more edge-case code examples focusing on formatting and trailing tokens (augment code-snippets by +800 prompts).
- Expand math-long-cot with adversarial carry cases and random-length intermediate steps (augment by +1000 examples).
- Add explicit separators to summarization prompts to test separator-sensitivity (A/B test with current production prompts).

Open questions / experiments to run:
- Is degradation in math-long-cot primarily due to KV precision or to layernorm/scale quantization? Run ablation quantizing only feedforward vs only attention weights.
- Can we get improved int4 stability by using a mixed AWQ/GPTQ pipeline (AWQ for attention weights, GPTQ for FFN)?
- Does prefix caching (reuse of early KV) amplify quantization noise across long documents? Need synthetic experiment controlling prefix reuse.

Short-term action items (owners + ETA):
- Marisa: schedule ablation (attention-only vs ffn-only quant) and produce result table (ETA 2025-03-05).
- Abe: add 800 code edge-case prompts to code-snippets set and run overnight eval (ETA 2025-03-03).
- Priya: prototype per-route auto-fallback check in Canary infra (ETA 2025-03-10).
- Sofia: open PR to try mixed AWQ/GPTQ config and push artifacts to s3 (ETA 2025-03-07).

Notes to self / TODOs:
- Capture seed and exact quantization config in CI artifacts (we had a missing seed for int4 run; replicate with deterministic seed).
- Add small visual diff tool showing token-level divergences heatmap for manual triage.

Appendix: quick reproducibility steps:
1) checkout branch models/pull/327
2) pip install -r requirements-eval.txt (use cuda 12.1 containers)
3) run: python eval/run_slice_evals.py --snapshot s3://redwood-evals/onboarding/2025-02-12/snapshot-20250212-17ac.tgz --variants int8-awq,int4-gptq --slices code-snippets,math-long-cot --out results/20250212
4) artifacts will include per-prompt outputs in JSONL and metrics summary CSV.

If you have immediate questions ping #eng-applied-ml or leave comments in the linked PR. This doc will be iterated as we get ablation results.
